newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Korean shares fall on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Korean shares fall on profit taking.

text.p: Korean global depositary receipts fell Friday, as investors took profits after a two-day ten percent rise, traders said.
"There have been some very good moves, and long-term the market looks expensive," a trader said.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index fell 4.00 points to 70.65 points, a premium of 38.23 percent over the local market.
The Seoul composite index rose 3.86 points to end the day at 746.36, the highest close so far this year.
Indian GDRs followed the local markets higher in a day with little volume, traders said.
Reliance gained 56 cent to $19.00/$19.50 in sympathy with a rise in the local market on fund buying, traders said.
The Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.68 points up at 81.96, with the premium over the local market at 25.48 percent from 25.31 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index closed up 32.06 points to 3,756.17.
The long-awaited hike in petroleum product prices is still hanging over the market, traders said, though a rise of about 20 percent is expected.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told local media on Thursday that a price increase was necessary but the issue needed to be thoroughly discussed among the partners in his centre-left coalition.
"It is not very good from anyone's point of view that the government can't seem to take hard decisions," a trader said.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 0.05 points, or 0.04 percent, to 114.88, representing a discount to the local market of 2.32 percent.
